675: /*
676:  * heap_oos_delete_unreferenced () - Eagerly delete the OOS records referenced by old_recdes and
677:  *   not referenced by new_recdes. new_recdes == NULL means none are referenced anymore (DELETE):
678:  *   every OOS OID of old_recdes is deleted unconditionally, which is safe because OOS OIDs are
679:  *   freshly allocated per heap record and never shared across rows. With a non-NULL new_recdes
680:  *   (UPDATE), OIDs present in both images (same physical OOS referenced before and after) are
681:  *   preserved.
682:  *
683:  * Called from the non-MVCC (!is_mvcc_op) branches of heap delete/update. For REC_RELOCATION rows
684:  * the caller passes the forward (REC_NEWHOME) record as old_recdes, because the actual data (and
685:  * OOS attributes) live on the forward page; the home slot holds only an 8-byte forwarding OID.
686:  *
687:  * MVCC mode keeps the old OOS alive for concurrent readers and lets vacuum reclaim it later;
688:  * SA_MODE has no readers and no vacuum, so deletion happens here or not at all. Despite the
689:  * historical "SA_MODE" tag in the diagnostics, the !is_mvcc_op gate also fires for SERVER_MODE
690:  * operations on MVCC-disabled classes (catalog tables), so this code can execute server-side too.
691:  * Caller MUST abort the transaction on error so oos_delete's per-chunk undo records replay any
692:  * partial deletes during rollback; otherwise the surviving recdes would reference already-deleted
693:  * OOS chunks.
694:  *
695:  * Strict failure handling: the OOS header flag is set by the record transformer and read via
696:  * heap_recdes_contains_oos, so a missing OOS file or a failed OID extraction at this point
697:  * indicates real corruption — log and propagate.
698:  *
699:  * Empty-page reclaim (oos_reclaim_empty_pages) must NOT be wired here: this runs inside a live
700:  * user transaction whose abort replays the per-chunk undo, and undo cannot re-insert chunks
701:  * into a deallocated page. Pages emptied here stay allocated.
